messages:
Priya: Heads-up: ACME is moving to contract stage. They want a POC for their claims-assistant. Traffic sketch below and they asked for a recommended committed GPU footprint + autoscale policy and a ballpark monthly commit+burst estimate to include in the commercial term sheet. Hoping for quick numbers to share at tomorrow sync.

Dan: Paste the traffic sample when you have it. Are they okay with Dedicated? Any constraint on latency or model family?

Priya: Quick profile they gave (their ops team):
```json
{
  \"avg_requests_per_min\": 100,
  \"peak_requests_per_min\": 500,
  \"peak_duration_seconds\": 90,
  \"peak_interval_minutes\": 12,
  \"avg_input_tokens\": 800,
  \"avg_output_tokens\": 200,
  \"p99_latency_ms\": 350,
  \"model_candidate\": \"redwood-vicuna-15b-like (int8)\",
  \"deployment_preference\": \"dedicated\"
}
```

Dan: Nice. Converting to tokens/sec: avg rps ~1.67 -> avg_tokens_s ~= 1.67 * 1000 = 1667 toks/s. Peak rps ~8.33 -> peak_tokens_s ~= 8333 toks/s. For a 15B-class int8 layout on our infra we usually see ~1.5-4 rps per GPU for 1000-token-ish requests depending on kernel set and batching.

Dan: Starter sizing (conservative):
- Commit suggestion: 3 reserved GPUs (H100 preferred) to cover steady state + modest headroom.
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas = 1 (for infra safety), reserved_replicas = 3, max_replicas = 8 (covers bursting and concurrency).
- Warm pool: keep 1 hot spare during business hours to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Burst strategy: enable rapid scale to max_replicas for up to 2 mins per burst; apply burst credits to minimize billing surprise.

Priya: Why 3 vs 2?

Dan: With conservative rps_per_gpu ~= 2 (for their token size and int8 path), 3 GPUs give ~6 rps sustained which maps to ~600 req/min effective when batching and cache hit help. Their average is 100 rpm so reserved 3 leaves runway for growth and avoids frequent scaling. Peaks to 500 rpm still require autoscale to 8 for the short windows.

InfraBot: Automated calc (inputs from profile):
- assumed_rps_per_gpu: 2
- reserved_gpus: 3
- max_gpus: 8
- reserved_gpu_hours/month: 3 * 24 * 30 = 2160 GPU-hours
- estimated_burst_on_demand_hours (assume 8% of time in peak windows at +5 GPUs): ~288 GPU-hours/month
Note: benching with the customer's real prompts may shift rps_per_gpu up or down.

Jorge: Pricing note 12: For a 12-month commit on 3 GPUs we can apply the standard committed discount (I'll generate a provisional quote). For burst usage we can offer a 10% discount on on-demand for enterprise agreements; confirm legal sign-off. I'll attach a draft USD/month figure later today.

Lina: Security/ops checklist items to surface to ACME: VPC peering and private endpoints, ability to use their KMS for key wrapping, optional FIPS modes if they require. Dedicated has audit-log export; retention and SIEM integration are negotiable. Also note network setup can add 5 business days on average.

Priya: Two requests: 1) Dan/infra team can you run a 90-minute perf run using 300 sample prompts (mixed-length) to validate rps_per_gpu? 2) Jorge can you produce a provisional line-item quote (commit + projected burst) including a 20% safety margin on consumption for commercial review?

Dan: I'll schedule a bench tomorrow morning. Please upload the sample set to the shared S3 path and grant infra read access. I'll also run with quantization toggles (int8 vs fp16) to see delta.

Jorge: On it. I9ll produce the provisional quote and put two options: (A) 3 GPU commit + on-demand bursts, (B) 4 GPU commit smaller burst cap (trade higher commit lower on-demand).

Lina: I'll DM Priya the onboarding checklist and expected timeline for VPC/KMS work.

Priya: Great 12 thanks all. I'll confirm the sample prompt upload and set the customer sync for Friday. :rocket:
